html:
The Temple of Garni is a Greco-Roman style temple with Ionic columns on a cliff above the Azat River east of Yerevan, built probably in the first century CE, likely by King Tiridates I of Armenia.

It may have been dedicated to the sun god Mihr. When Armenia adopted Christianity around 301, pagan temples were destroyed, but Garni was spared, perhaps as a royal summer house. It collapsed in an earthquake in 1679 and was rebuilt from its original stones in the 1970s. Nearby are a royal bath with a mosaic floor and the fortress of Garni. It is the only standing temple of its kind in the former Soviet lands and a centre of the modern Armenian pagan revival. The nearby Geghard monastery is cut into the rock.
sum: The Temple of Garni is a Greco-Roman style temple with Ionic columns on a cliff above the Azat River east of Yerevan, built probably in the first century CE, likely by King Tiridates I of Armenia.
